text: The rwb-partner clearance read, the rwb-case state read and case-move answer, the rwb-access authorise call and the rwb-decision package read are consumed on their owners' published contracts, never as tables or views, and their operation names stay placeholders until the owners publish them.
why: Only rwb-partner holds the panel and buyer facts, only rwb-case writes recovery_case, only rwb-access answers the right and only rwb-decision governs the rule rows. TSD S6 T5.2 names the module interfaces without an operation name, so no name may be invented; the plan's C row for the slice is empty, so the rows are C dependencies in fact and not in the metadata.
read: FSD S6 A2.8.2 and A2.8.3.1; TSD S6 T5.2 and T-A.1; context pack S6 ownership rows; Template and Rules v1 R5.4 class C and R5.5 DP-11
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6004-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 11, 12.2 and 13; RWB-S6-E6004-CON sections 3, 7 AC3, 11, 12.2 and 13
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-partner, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision, before the contract is tagged
impact: The app story builds on Day 1 against five contract fakes with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and a statement on a partner, recovery_case or role row fails the boundary test

text: The capability area and the right of each surface are declared and checked through the service-template guard; DP-08 is not added to the pattern set or to the metadata, and no outbox row is written by this step although DP-09 is also absent.
why: The plan gives DP03, DP13 and DP19 for this key, while the provided operation declares the Partner portal right C and the service owns a topic with the outbox and inbox library. Adding a pattern or a dependency row would invent a plan value, so both are named in the text and recorded as absent.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-08, DP-09 and DP-14; TSD S6 T6.1 and T6.2; context pack S6 (topic and platform library rules)
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6004-APP sections 3, 8 BR8, 10, 12.7, 12.9 and 13; RWB-S6-E6004-CON sections 7 AC3, 8 BR5, 10 and 13
confirm: Solution architect and the platform library owner, before wave 4 starts
impact: The right is enforced per surface by the template guard and the library object outbox_event exists unused at this step; the two rows are tracked rather than added to the metadata

text: The bid submission API-S6-005 POST /partner/data-room/{lotId}/bids is provided by RWB-S6-E6004-APP on the debt sale base, additively within major version 1 of the fragment the data room story publishes, because it is the take-bids deliverable of this legacy key and no sibling story builds it.
why: TSD S6 T-A.1 publishes the operation with the Partner portal C right and gives it 'first in E5', while RWB-S6-E5026-CON names the bid as another story's and RWB-S6-E6005-APP names it as the data room story's, so the sources contradict each other. The legacy story of this key is the one that takes bids, and every sibling declares the operation as not built by it, so one story has to own it.
read: TSD S6 T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD S6 A2.8.2 (integration points: partner portal); legacy RWB-E6-004 Endpoints; sibling story files RWB-S6-E5026-CON, RWB-S6-E6005-APP and RWB-S6-E6009-APP
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6004-APP sections 1, 4, 7, 12.1 and 13; RWB-S6-E6004-CON sections 1, 7 AC1, 12.1 and 13
confirm: Solution architect with the data room and award story owners, before the contract is tagged
impact: One operation is published once, the two legacy endpoint rows stay with RWB-S6-E6005-APP and RWB-S6-E5026-APP, and a duplicate provision fails the review

text: The bid amount, the bid time and the bid reference are held in the decision record and the idempotency row, and the realized recovery is written on debt_sale_account.selling_price; no column is added by this story and no total is computed or invented.
why: R-DS-18 records a bid against the lot and the buyer and R-DS-34 records realized recovery by lot and by buyer, but TSD S6 T3.1 declares neither a bid amount, a bid time or a bid reference nor a realized-recovery total. Writing a value into a column the model does not have, or summing one from nowhere, would invent a business fact.
read: TSD S6 T3.1 (DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-037); FSD S6 A2.8.3.2 field catalog; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-18 and R-DS-34
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6004-APP sections 2, 4, 7, 8 BR5, 11, 12.7 and 13; RWB-S6-E6004-CON sections 7 AC2 and AC4, 8 BR7, 11 and 12.7
confirm: Data steward and the solution architect when the column set of the module is extended
impact: The bid amount and its time are recoverable from the decision record, the realized recovery is readable per account, and no undocumented column is created

text: This story owns R-DS-18 and the no-claim branch of R-DS-34 for its legacy key; the claim branch of R-DS-35 and the close after a refused claim of R-DS-39 stay with RWB-S6-E6009-APP, and RWB-S6-E6002-APP keeps R-DS-18 tabled, so one writer per rule is fixed at assembly.
why: Legacy RWB-E6-004 owns AC2 as R-DS-34 and legacy RWB-E6-002 AC3 and RWB-E6-009 AC3 name R-DS-18 and R-DS-34 as well, so the split stories of three keys declare the same two rows. The bid operation, the bid fact and the close on a lot with no claim are this story's deliverable, so it cannot hand them away without losing its criteria, and the claim path is the put-back story's behaviour.
read: legacy RWB-E6-004 AC2; legacy RWB-E6-002 AC3; legacy RWB-E6-009 AC3; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-18, R-DS-34, R-DS-35 and R-DS-39; TSD S6 T4
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6004-APP sections 2, 7, 8 and 19; RWB-S6-E6004-CON sections 2, 8 BR11 and 19
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of RWB-S6-E6002-APP and RWB-S6-E6009-APP at assembly
impact: Each rule has one writing story, the claim path does not close a lot behind this story's back, and the duplicate declarations are reconciled in the register

text: The realized recovery of a closed lot is written to this service's rows and its decision record; the 'Recovery Data Store' and 'Power BI' destinations of R-DS-34 are not built, no lot-closure event is published because no catalogue entry carries one, and rwb-reporting's read model is fed by the events of the award and transfer steps.
why: There is no data lake and no Power BI feed in the target, DP-17 is not in the pattern set of this key and TSD S6 T5.3 declares only LotAwarded for the module. Inventing an event or a reporting table would create a business value no source carries, and claiming the reporting read model would take another service's deliverable.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17; TSD S6 T5.3; context pack S6 (no data lake; rwb-reporting builds its read model from events); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DS-34
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6004-APP sections 2, 8 BR10, 12.3, 12.4 and 19; RWB-S6-E6004-CON sections 7 AC5, 8 BR12, 12.3 and 19
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-reporting owner when the reporting read model is specified
impact: The closure leaves its evidence in the service's own rows and the decision record, the absence of a closure event is a recorded gap, and no data-lake or Power BI work is scheduled

text: The story keeps wave 4 because EP06 is the wave 4 business epic, while rwb-debtsale is created in wave 3; the conflict is recorded once for the service and the business epic and the release date stays 30 April 2027 (tentative).
why: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 keeps the W-MAP wave of a story when it is later than the service's Arch v5 wave, and the split plan gives wave 4 for this slice. Neither a date nor a wave may be changed by a story builder, and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.6 and U7; split plan slice RWB-S6-E6004-APP (wave 4, release 30 April 2027); context pack S6 (service wave 3)
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6004-APP metadata and section 2; RWB-S6-E6004-CON metadata and section 2
confirm: Release manager at the wave gate
impact: The story is planned in wave 4 and no date is moved

text: No programme requirement id is carried for this slice; the nearest rows, REQ-S6-004 (a buyer check before bidding) and REQ-S6-006 (the award), belong to the sibling keys, so the traceability table cites the placeholder and the PRD (C1) allocates a requirement for taking the bid.
why: SPLIT plan gives the slice an empty requirement list, the programme and FSD requirement tables carry no row for taking a bid or for closing a lot on the claim window, and adopting a neighbour's id would misstate the trace.
read: split plan slice RWB-S6-E6004-APP (reqs empty); Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-S6-001 to REQ-S6-009; FSD S6 Requirements served; TSD S6 T8
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6004-APP sections 2 and 18; RWB-S6-E6004-CON sections 7 AC1, 11 and 18

text: The bid window, the claim window, the reserve and the tiered terms are values of the Debt sale rule package and of reference data, read at their version in force; the claim window is a durable timer of the workflow and its length stays unpublished until the package is baselined.
why: R-DS-34 carries the timer 'per claim window' and R-DS-17 the timer 'per cycle', and no source gives either a length. Writing a duration in code or in the test data would fix a business value that a business person may change, which the legacy guardrails forbid.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DS-17 and R-DS-34; TSD S6 T3.2 and T4; FSD S6 BR-S6-008; legacy RWB-E6-004 Guardrails
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6004-APP sections 3, 4, 8 BR7, 13 and 14; RWB-S6-E6004-CON sections 7 AC5, 8 BR11 and 12.6
confirm: Rule owner in rwb-decision and the debt sale business owner when the package is baselined
impact: Changing a window or a term is a package change with a version, not a code change, and the tests read the values from the fake package

text: The bid arrives from a partner organisation through the partner gateway in the DMZ in front of rwb-partner, scoped to the buyer's own lots, and that channel has no story row in the plan, so it is served by the same operation through the gateway and its identity, sign-in and route are recorded as missing.
why: The legacy permission table gives the Partner portal right R to internal roles with a long role list, the RBAC matrix gives PT-BUYER RU scoped to its own lots, and no story of this service, no platform contract story and no external row of this slice owns the partner gateway. Building it here would take an edge owner's deliverable.
read: TSD S6 T6.1 (PT-BUYER RU) and T6.2; FSD S6 A2.8.2 (integration points: partner portal); context pack S6 (partner gateway in the DMZ); legacy RWB-E6-004 Permission checks
applied_in: RWB-S6-E6004-APP sections 2, 4, 10, 12.8, 15 and 19; RWB-S6-E6004-CON sections 7 AC5, 8 BR13, 12.8, 12.9 and 15
confirm: Solution architect and the edge owner when the partner channel is planned
impact: The operation is reachable by the buyer through the gateway, the staff screens read the same element through the composite route, and no partner channel code is built in this service
